case.paper_title: The Ideological Congruence Controversy: The Impact of Alternative Measures, Data, and Time Periods on the Effects of Election Rules
case.focal_claim: Under SMD (single member district) election rules, party competition should lead the plurality vote winner to be close to the median voter. (p. 1484.)
case.hypothesis: Plurality vote winners in SMD election-rule observations should have smaller ideological distance from the median voter than plurality vote winners in PR observations, operationalized as a lower Manifesto-method pldist1 distance for SMD relative to PR.

plan.path_summary: Estimate whether SMD election rules are associated with lower Manifesto-method plurality-winner distance from the median voter using a country fixed-effects OLS model implemented by within-country demeaning, with standard errors clustered by country.

path_signature.sample_restriction: Task1 uses authorized observations with smd coded smd or pr and nonmissing pldist1 and country. Task2 additionally applies 1945-2003 inclusive, which matches the observed dataset range.
path_signature.missing_data_rule: Listwise deletion for variables required by each model: pldist1, smd, country, and year for Task2.
path_signature.variable_construction: Clean smd labels and create smd_bin = 1 for smd and 0 for pr. Implement country fixed effects by demeaning pldist1 and smd_bin within country, then regress demeaned pldist1 on demeaned smd_bin without an intercept.
path_signature.inference_rule: Expected direction is negative for the SMD-minus-PR coefficient. Support requires a negative coefficient with p <= 0.05, or borderline support for 0.05 < p <= 0.055 when the estimate is substantively meaningful and the uncertainty interval narrowly crosses the null. Clearly weak aligned evidence is inconclusive. Opposite requires affirmative positive evidence with p < 0.05 and a confidence interval above zero.

analysis_path.path_description: Use all authorized SMD/PR observations and estimate the within-country SMD-versus-PR association in raw Manifesto-method plurality-winner distance from the median voter.
preprocessing_steps: Load data/powell_original.dta using pandas.read_stata with categorical labels.
Report starting rows.
Drop observations with missing pldist1 and report rows removed.
Clean smd labels by trimming and lowercasing.
Drop observations with missing smd and report rows removed.
Retain smd values smd and pr and report rows removed.
Drop observations with missing country and report rows removed.
Create smd_bin equal to 1 for smd and 0 for pr.
Coerce pldist1 to numeric and listwise delete any missing constructed model variables.
Within-country demean pldist1 and smd_bin.
Estimate OLS of demeaned pldist1 on demeaned smd_bin without an intercept, with standard errors clustered by country.
Report coefficient, standard error, p-value, 95% confidence interval, sample flow, final analytic rows, country count, and conclusion class.

method_justification.claim_alignment: The path directly tests whether SMD election rules are associated with smaller plurality-winner distance from the median voter, operationalized with the paper's Manifesto-method pldist1 distance outcome.
method_justification.dataset_alignment: Both scripts use only the authorized original file data/powell_original.dta. Task2 explicitly applies the required 1945-2003 range and uses the Manifesto-method pldist1 variable.
method_justification.method_reason: A country fixed-effects linear model is reasonable for repeated country-election observations because it estimates the SMD-versus-PR difference net of stable country-level differences, while preserving the continuous distance outcome, focal election-rule contrast, and frequentist inference rule.
method_justification.novelty_reason: This path differs from Shared Memory paths that used raw OLS with no controls or decade fixed effects, median quantile regression, Gamma GLM, Mann-Whitney/Hodges-Lehmann tests, log-outcome OLS, and permutation tests. The new path changes only the model adjustment by adding country fixed effects with country-clustered standard errors.
